items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I don't know, I suppose somebody like Helen Merrill... [INTERVIEWEE] It does.

ctx.x: the home town don't appreciate them. Sometimes you go to these towns and you hear the musicians and if you're from out of town and you dare to bring out your horn, I mean, they'll play rings around you. So, I don't know, now that everybody is traveling more and should travel more, that they should get around to hear other music, really, because everybody isn't on record, everybody isn't on the radio and it's worse now.

I mean, this seems to be the case especially in jazz singers. I don't know, I suppose somebody like Helen Merrill, you know, it seems to me, I haven't studied her career very carefully but it seems to me she made a whole bunch of records in the 1950s and dropped out of sight for a long long time. And then maybe, I think in the '60s she recorded with Teddy Wilson and then dropped out again, you know. And that happens time and time again with people.
